learn.hook: To tell an electrician exactly where a bulb hangs in a room, you need three numbers: how far along, how far across, and how high. Welcome to 3-D.
points: A point on a plane needs two coordinates; a point in space (a bulb hanging in a room) needs three.
Take three mutually perpendicular lines through a point O: the x-axis, y-axis and z-axis. O is the origin.
The axes determine three coordinate planes: the XY-plane (contains the x- and y-axes), the YZ-plane and the ZX-plane.
The three coordinate planes divide space into eight parts called octants.
Octants are named XOYZ, X′OYZ, X′OY′Z, XOY′Z, XOYZ′, X′OYZ′, X′OY′Z′, XOY′Z′ — numbered I to VIII.

example.q: How many octants, coordinate planes and coordinate axes are there in 3-D space?
steps: Three axes x, y, z through O.
Each pair of axes makes a coordinate plane: XY, YZ, ZX — three planes.
Three planes cut space into 8 octants.

learn.reallife: Air-traffic control at Delhi airport tracks each plane by two ground coordinates plus altitude — a point in 3-D space.

games.title: Space basics
items: Three coordinate planes divide space into 8 octants.
Each plane splits space in two: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
The coordinate axes in 3-D are mutually perpendicular.
Each pair of axes meets at right angles at O.
The z-axis is perpendicular to the XY-plane, meeting it only at O.
A point in space needs exactly two coordinates.
It needs three: x, y and z.
The XY-plane and the YZ-plane meet along the y-axis.

quiz.q: How many octants are formed by the three coordinate planes?
quiz.explain: Each of the three planes divides space into two halves: 2³ = 8 octants.
steps: Each coordinate plane splits space into two halves
quiz.mistake: Uses the 4 quadrants of the plane

quiz.q: The z-axis is perpendicular to which coordinate plane?
quiz.explain: The XY-plane contains the x- and y-axes, both perpendicular to the z-axis.
steps: The XY-plane contains the x- and y-axes
The z-axis is perpendicular to both of these axes
So it is perpendicular to the plane that holds them
quiz.mistake: Picks a plane that contains the z-axis

quiz.q: The coordinate planes XY and ZX intersect along the:
quiz.explain: The x-axis is common to both the XY-plane and the ZX-plane.
steps: XY-plane contains the x- and y-axes; ZX-plane contains the z- and x-axes
The axis in both lists is x
Two planes meet along their common axis
quiz.mistake: Picks the axis missing from both names

quiz.q: Why does a point in space need three coordinates?
options: Because the plane has three axes
Because one coordinate is always zero
Space has three independent directions: length, breadth and height
quiz.explain: Two numbers fix a position on a floor; the third fixes the height above it.
steps: Length and breadth fix a position on a floor (2 numbers)
Height above the floor needs a third number
Answer: Space has three independent directions: length, breadth and height
quiz.mistake: Thinks the number of coordinates depends on the octants

quiz.q: How many coordinate planes are there in 3-D geometry?
quiz.explain: XY, YZ and ZX.
steps: Each plane contains two of the three axes
Pairs: x & y, y & z, z & x
That gives XY, YZ and ZX
quiz.mistake: Counts the octants

quiz.q: Octant I (XOYZ) is bounded by:
options: the positive x-, y- and z-axes
quiz.explain: XOYZ uses OX, OY and OZ, the positive directions of all three axes.
steps: XOYZ is named by the rays OX, OY and OZ
OX, OY, OZ are the positive directions of the axes
So octant I lies between the positive axes
Bounded by the positive x-, y- and z-axes
Answer: the positive x-, y- and z-axes
quiz.mistake: Forgets the z-direction

quiz.q: Which line is common to all three coordinate planes?
options: None — they share only the origin
quiz.explain: Each pair of planes shares an axis, but no single line lies in all three; only O is common to all.
steps: XY ∩ YZ = y-axis, YZ ∩ ZX = z-axis, ZX ∩ XY = x-axis
No axis lies in all three planes
Only O is common to all three
Answer: None — they share only the origin
quiz.mistake: Thinks one axis lies in every plane

quiz.q: In a room, take one corner of the floor as the origin with two floor edges as the x- and y-axes. The vertical edge at that corner is the:
quiz.explain: The vertical edge is perpendicular to both floor edges, so it is the z-axis.
steps: The two floor edges are the x- and y-axes
The vertical edge is perpendicular to both of them
The third axis, perpendicular to x and y, is the z-axis
The vertical edge is the z-axis
quiz.mistake: Treats the vertical edge as a plane

teach.ask: Gappu is used to graph paper with 2 axes. Explain how 3 axes, 3 coordinate planes and 8 octants describe space.
teach.praise: Three perpendicular axes, three planes, eight octants. Space is my new graph paper!
teach.nudge: How many parts do the three coordinate planes cut space into?

revise.summary: Three mutually perpendicular axes through the origin O give three coordinate planes (XY, YZ, ZX), which divide space into eight octants. A point in space needs three coordinates.
focus: Name the three axes, three coordinate planes and eight octants
Identify which axis is perpendicular to which plane and where planes meet
Explain why space needs three coordinates
remember: 3 axes (x, y, z), 3 coordinate planes (XY, YZ, ZX), 8 octants
The z-axis is perpendicular to the XY-plane
Octant I (XOYZ) uses the positive x-, y- and z-axes
traps: There are 3 coordinate planes, not 8: the 8 are octants
No single line lies in all three coordinate planes; only the origin is common

topics.title: Coordinates of a point in space

learn.hook: (2, −3, 5): go 2 along x, 3 backwards along y, 5 up. The signs tell you instantly which octant the point lives in.
points: The coordinates (x, y, z) of P are its (signed) perpendicular distances from the YZ-, ZX- and XY-planes respectively.
On the x-axis: (x, 0, 0); on the y-axis: (0, y, 0); on the z-axis: (0, 0, z). The origin is (0, 0, 0).
In the XY-plane: (x, y, 0); in the YZ-plane: (0, y, z); in the ZX-plane: (x, 0, z).
A point with any coordinate 0 lies on a coordinate plane (or axis), not inside an octant.

example.q: In which octants do (1, −2, 3) and (−4, 2, −5) lie?

learn.reallife: A warehouse robot in an e-commerce fulfilment centre locates a shelf bin by (aisle, rack, level) — three coordinates.

quiz.q: In which octant does (−3, 1, 2) lie?
quiz.explain: Signs (−, +, +) give octant II (X′OYZ).
steps: So the point is in X′OYZ
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the x-sign

quiz.q: In which octant does (−4, −2, −5) lie?
quiz.explain: All three negative: octant VII.
steps: All three negative is octant VII
quiz.mistake: Mixes up octants III and VII

quiz.q: A point lies on the x-axis. Which of its coordinates are zero?
quiz.explain: Every point on the x-axis has the form (x, 0, 0).
steps: Points on the x-axis have the form (x, 0, 0)
So the y- and z-coordinates are 0
quiz.mistake: Thinks the coordinate named after the axis is zero

quiz.q: A point lies in the YZ-plane. Its coordinates have the form:
quiz.explain: The YZ-plane is x = 0.
steps: The YZ-plane is the plane x = 0
y and z can take any values
So points look like (0, y, z)
quiz.mistake: Sets y and z to zero instead

quiz.q: The perpendicular distance of P(3, −4, 5) from the XY-plane is:
quiz.explain: Distance from the XY-plane is |z| = 5.
quiz.mistake: Uses the x-coordinate

quiz.q: The foot of the perpendicular from P(3, −4, 5) to the ZX-plane is:
quiz.explain: The ZX-plane is y = 0, so the foot keeps x and z and makes y = 0.
steps: The foot keeps x and z and sets y = 0
quiz.mistake: Makes the wrong coordinate zero

quiz.q: Which point lies in octant VIII?
quiz.explain: Octant VIII has signs (+, −, −).
steps: The other options have the wrong signs
quiz.mistake: Uses the order of signs for octant VI or V

quiz.q: Which point lies on a coordinate plane, not in any octant?
quiz.explain: y = 0 puts (5, 0, −2) on the ZX-plane.
steps: A point is on a coordinate plane if one coordinate is 0
(5, 0, −2) has y = 0, so it lies on the ZX-plane
The other points have no zero coordinate
quiz.mistake: Thinks negative coordinates mean 'outside every octant'

teach.ask: Gappu found the point (−2, 3, −4) and wants to know where it is. Explain what the three coordinates mean and how signs give the octant.
teach.praise: Each coordinate is a signed distance from a plane, and the three signs pick the octant. (−, +, −) is octant VI!
teach.nudge: What do the signs of x, y and z tell you about a point?

revise.summary: The coordinates (x, y, z) of a point are its signed distances from the YZ-, ZX- and XY-planes. Points on an axis or a coordinate plane have zeros, and the signs of x, y, z decide the octant.
focus: Find the octant of a point from its signs
Write the form of points on axes and coordinate planes
Find distances from coordinate planes and feet of perpendiculars
remember: x, y, z: distances from the YZ-, ZX- and XY-planes
x-axis: (x, 0, 0); XY-plane: (x, y, 0); YZ-plane: (0, y, z); ZX-plane: (x, 0, z)
traps: The distance from the XY-plane is |z|, not √(x² + y² + z²)
A point with a zero coordinate is on a plane or axis, not inside an octant

topics.title: Distance between two points in space

learn.hook: How long a cable do you need from a ceiling corner to the opposite floor corner? The 3-D distance formula is Pythagoras applied twice.
points: PQ = √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)² + (z₂ − z₁)²).
Derivation: draw a box with PQ as a diagonal; Pythagoras in the base gives PN² = (x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)², then PQ² = PN² + (z₂ − z₁)².
Distance from the origin: OP = √(x² + y² + z²).
Collinearity: P, Q, R are collinear if one distance equals the sum of the other two (e.g. PQ + QR = PR).
Syllabus note: the section formula in 3-D is not part of the current rationalised syllabus for this chapter.

example.q: Show that A(1, 2, 3), B(2, 3, 4) and C(4, 5, 6) are collinear.
example.answer: Collinear, with B between A and C

learn.reallife: Architects in Mumbai's high-rises compute diagonal lengths of rooms for cables and ducts using √(l² + b² + h²).

games.title: Derive the 3-D distance formula
items: Draw a cuboid with PQ as a diagonal
In the base, PN² = (x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²
QN is vertical, so triangle PNQ is right-angled at N

quiz.q: Find the distance between (2, −1, 3) and (−2, 1, 3).
quiz.mistake: Adds the differences instead of squaring

quiz.q: The distance of (6, −2, 3) from the origin is:
quiz.mistake: Forgets to square the negative coordinate

quiz.q: A room is 4 m long, 3 m wide and 12 m high (a tall atrium). What is the length of the longest straight rod that fits?
quiz.explain: The space diagonal is √(16 + 9 + 144) = √169 = 13 m.
steps: Longest rod = space diagonal = √(l² + b² + h²)
quiz.mistake: Uses only the floor diagonal

quiz.q: For P(1, 0, 2), Q(2, 1, 4) and R(4, 3, 8), PQ = √6 and QR = 2√6. What is PR, and are the points collinear?
quiz.explain: PR = √(9 + 9 + 36) = √54 = 3√6 = PQ + QR, so the points are collinear.
quiz.mistake: Compares only two of the three distances

quiz.q: If the distance between (k, 2, 1) and (1, 2, 1) is 3, which can k be?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the absolute value and takes k = 3

quiz.q: Which points are at distance 5 from the origin?
steps: Distance from the origin = √(x² + y² + z²)
quiz.mistake: Adds the coordinates

quiz.q: The distance of P(3, 4, 5) from the z-axis is:
quiz.explain: The nearest point on the z-axis is (0, 0, 5); distance √(9 + 16) = 5.
steps: The nearest point on the z-axis to (3, 4, 5) is (0, 0, 5)
quiz.mistake: Uses the z-coordinate as the distance

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): A(0, 0, 0), B(1, 1, 1) and C(2, 2, 2) are collinear.
Reason (R): AB + BC = AC.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
quiz.explain: AB = √3, BC = √3, AC = 2√3 = AB + BC. That equality is exactly the test for collinearity.
steps: AB + BC = 2√3 = AC, so R is true
That equality is the collinearity test, so A is true
Answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.mistake: Does not connect the distance sum to collinearity

teach.ask: Gappu needs the length of a cable from one corner of his room's floor to the opposite ceiling corner. Explain the 3-D distance formula.
teach.praise: Square all three differences, add, take the root. Pythagoras goes 3-D!
teach.nudge: How many differences do you square in 3-D, and what do you do after adding them?

revise.summary: The distance between P(x₁, y₁, z₁) and Q(x₂, y₂, z₂) is √((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)² + (z₂ − z₁)²), and from the origin it is √(x² + y² + z²). Three points are collinear if one distance equals the sum of the other two.
focus: Find distances between points and from the origin
Use the space diagonal √(l² + b² + h²) of a box
Test collinearity using PQ + QR = PR
Find an unknown coordinate from a given distance (two answers)
remember: Collinear if PQ + QR = PR (one distance is the sum of the other two)
traps: Square the differences before adding; don't add the differences first
|k − 1| = 3 has two answers, k = 4 and k = −2

learn.hook: With just the distance formula you can prove a triangle is right-angled, find a missing corner of a parallelogram and even write the equation of a surface.
points: Triangle type: compute all three sides. Right-angled if the squares satisfy Pythagoras; isosceles if two sides are equal; equilateral if all three are equal.
Parallelogram ABCD: opposite sides equal (AB = CD, BC = DA). The missing vertex D = A + C − B (coordinate-wise), since the diagonals bisect each other.
Locus of P equidistant from A and B: PA² = PB²; the squared terms cancel, leaving a plane (the perpendicular bisector plane).
Locus of P with PA + PB = constant 2a (A, B the foci): an ellipsoid. With foci (±c, 0, 0): x²/a² + (y² + z²)/(a² − c²) = 1.
Points on an axis at a given distance: e.g. on the y-axis use (0, y, 0) and solve.

example.q: Find the equation of the set of points P equidistant from A(1, 0, 2) and B(3, 0, 0).
steps: Expand and cancel x², y², z²: −2x + 1 − 4z + 4 = −6x + 9.

learn.reallife: A drone delivery hub placed equidistant from two warehouses must lie on the perpendicular bisector plane of the line joining them.

pairs: Sum of squares of two sides = square of third

Triangle A(1, 0, 0), B(0, 1, 0), C(0, 0, 1) has every side ___
On the y-axis, points at distance 13 from (3, 4, 12) have y = 0 or ___

quiz.explain: AB = BC = CA = √2.
quiz.mistake: Assumes a 'corner' triangle is right-angled

quiz.q: Are A(0, 0, 0), B(3, 0, 0), C(3, 4, 0) the vertices of a right triangle?
quiz.explain: AB = 3, BC = 4, AC = 5 and 3² + 4² = 5², so the right angle is opposite AC, at B.
steps: The right angle is opposite the longest side AC, i.e. at B
quiz.mistake: Places the right angle at the origin

quiz.q: The fourth vertex D of parallelogram ABCD with A(1, 2, 3), B(3, 4, 5), C(6, 5, 4) is:
steps: Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so D = A + C − B
quiz.mistake: Uses A + B − C instead

quiz.q: The locus of points equidistant from A(2, 0, 0) and B(0, 0, 2) is:
quiz.explain: (x − 2)² + y² + z² = x² + y² + (z − 2)² ⇒ −4x = −4z ⇒ x = z.
steps: PA² = PB²: (x − 2)² + y² + z² = x² + y² + (z − 2)²
quiz.mistake: Keeps the squared terms

quiz.q: The length of the median from A(2, 0, 0) in triangle ABC with B(0, 4, 0), C(0, 0, 6) is:
quiz.explain: Midpoint of BC is (0, 2, 3). Distance from A = √(4 + 4 + 9) = √17.
steps: Median from A goes to the midpoint of BC: ((0 + 0)/2, (4 + 0)/2, (0 + 6)/2) = (0, 2, 3)
quiz.mistake: Measures from A to B or C instead of the midpoint

quiz.q: Points on the y-axis at distance 13 from (3, 4, 12) are:
quiz.mistake: Keeps only one root

quiz.q: The locus of P such that PA + PB = 10, where A = (3, 0, 0) and B = (−3, 0, 0), is:
quiz.mistake: Swaps the denominators

quiz.explain: AC = √(1 + 4 + 4) = 3, BC = √(1 + 4 + 4) = 3 and AB = 2. Two sides are equal, and 2² + 3² ≠ 3², so it is isosceles but not right-angled.
steps: AC = BC, so two sides are equal
quiz.mistake: Stops before checking all three sides

teach.ask: Gappu wants to prove three points in space make a right triangle and to find the plane of points equidistant from two towers. Explain how.
teach.praise: Three distances settle the triangle type, and PA² = PB² gives a neat plane. 3-D detective work!
teach.nudge: To find points equidistant from A and B, which equation do you write?

revise.summary: Use the distance formula to classify triangles and check parallelograms, and find a missing vertex with D = A + C − B. Points equidistant from A and B form a plane; points with PA + PB = 2a form an ellipsoid.
focus: Classify triangles in space by their side lengths
Find the fourth vertex of a parallelogram
Find the locus of points equidistant from two points
Find points on an axis at a given distance
remember: Right triangle: squares of sides satisfy Pythagoras; isosceles: two equal sides; equilateral: all equal
Parallelogram ABCD: D = A + C − B (coordinate-wise)
PA² = PB² gives a plane (squared terms cancel)
PA + PB = 2a with foci (±c, 0, 0): x²/a² + (y² + z²)/(a² − c²) = 1
traps: The right angle is at the vertex opposite the longest side
Check Pythagoras before calling an isosceles triangle right-angled
